title: What If the Sun Flipped Its Magnetic Poles?

scenes.text: What if the Sun flipped its magnetic poles? It already does, every eleven years.
The field weakens to zero, then rebuilds pointing the opposite way, over a matter of months.
It happens at the peak of the solar cycle, with more sunspots, flares and eruptions.
A giant sheet of electric current spreads out from the Sun's equator. During the flip, it gets wavy.
Earth dips in and out of that sheet, which can bring stormy space weather and disrupt satellites.
The ripples could also shield astronauts better from cosmic rays. NASA calls the flip a regular part of the solar cycle.
